newsitem.title: UK: Standard Chartered up on upbeat comment.
newsitem.headline: Standard Chartered up on upbeat comment.

text.p: Shares in Standard Chartered Plc rose in early trading on Friday after positive comment in the influencial Lex column of the Financial Times, traders said.
The stock, which has come under pressure in recent sessions amid a series of negative analyst comments, was up 10-1/2p at 662-1/2 by 0719 GMT.
Standard shares yesterday closed at their lowest level for three months.

The FT said the recent decline in the stock had not taken sufficient account of the company's position as a growth stock with excellent prospects across south east Asia and that the "current spell of weakness looks like a buying opportunity."

"The shares have come off about ten percent and the profit downgrades have been much more modest," said Nick Collier, banking analyst at Morgan Stanley, adding that the company still had growth potential.
Morgan Stanley said they rated the stock "outperform".
